method: Run scripts/jetson_track_review.py twice from frame 1 with persistent tracking. Compare per-frame JSONL track IDs and inspect annotated frames 75-77 at the scene cut. The replay has four static source images with a slight synthetic zoom and no ground-truth identities.

observed_difference.frame_75: Default and no-GMC both assign ID 8 to a bottle-transp in scene 1.
observed_difference.frame_76: A hard cut starts scene 2. Default assigns the can ID 8; no-GMC detects the can without a track ID.
observed_difference.frame_77: Default keeps ID 8 on the can; no-GMC assigns the can new ID 24.
observed_difference.within_scene: The runs have the same per-scene ID counts and frame-by-frame class counts. After relabeling IDs by scene, the per-frame object-to-ID associations are the same apart from frame 76's untracked can.
observed_difference.decision_effect: With a persistent seen-ID set across the replay, new_decisions would emit 27 first-ID events for default and 28 for no-GMC. Default would suppress the can as a new proposed decision because ID 8 was already seen on the bottle.

limits: This is a synthetic replay with hard cuts and no physical-object identity labels. It cannot establish ID-switch rate on a real moving conveyor, and this review run writes MP4 so it is not a speed measurement.
